subject: Onward transfer: conditional approval for CyberLytics subprocessors
messages:
From: Elena Morales <emorales@cyberlytics.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, contracts@cyberlytics.com
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Request: onward transfer permission and roster (CyberLytics -> Redwood)

Hi Jasmine and Marissa,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our integration checklist for the Redwood platform, CyberLytics is submitting our current subprocessor roster and a brief dataflow map for any onward transfers. Please confirm whether you require:

- A formal explicit permission for onward transfers to downstream analytics processors (we use DataLakeX for aggregated metrics)
- Evidence of SOC 2 or equivalent for our analytics provider
- Any template SCCs / DPA addenda we need to sign for EU flows

Attached: initial roster (PDF) and a high-level dataflow diagram (XLSX). Happy to jump on a call if helpful.

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Legal Ops
CyberLytics
Attachments: cyberlytics_subproc_roster_v2.pdf (application/pdf), dataflow-mapping.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <emorales@cyberlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, alex_martinez@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: onward transfer permission and roster (CyberLytics -> Redwood)

Hi Elena — thanks for sending these over and for the clear attachments. Quick heads-up on process so expectations are aligned:

1) We generally evaluate downstream subprocessors for two outcomes: full approval, or conditional approval (limited to non-production data and aggregated telemetry) pending evidence.
2) Required evidence to avoid a conditional approval typically includes a recent SOC 2 Type II report (redacted copy acceptable), data-at-rest encryption details, and confirmation of whether downstream vendors process EU personal data (SCCs may be required).

Can you confirm:
- Whether DataLakeX stores any customer PII or only aggregated/hashed metrics
- If CyberLytics can sign standard SCCs for EU flows if needed

I’ve cc'd Alex from product and Marissa from Privacy so they can weigh in on operational impact. If you can send the SOC 2 report and confirm the DataLakeX scope, we can aim for a decision within 3 business days.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Security & Compliance Analyst | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Elena Morales <emorales@cyberlytics.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, contracts@cyberlytics.com
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: onward transfer permission and roster (CyberLytics -> Redwood)

Hi Jasmine — thank you, and apologies for the delay. Clarifications below:

- DataLakeX is used for aggregated metrics and long-term analytics. It does receive hashed identifiers and occasionally pseudonymized session metadata. We do not store raw customer PII there.
- We can sign SCCs for EU personal data flows; happy to review Redwood's standard language.

I've attached the more detailed roster and a slightly expanded dataflow that highlights DataLakeX and a backup cloud logging provider. Also attaching a redacted SOC 2 summary; the full report requires an NDA but we can provide a redacted copy for your review.

Attachments: cyberlytics_subproc_roster_v2.pdf, dataflow-mapping.xlsx

Let us know if the redacted SOC summary is sufficient or if you need the full report under NDA.

Regards,
Elena
From: alex_martinez@redwood.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: onward transfer permission and roster (CyberLytics -> Redwood)

Jasmine / Marissa — reviewed the roster and the dataflow. High level: no immediate blocker but recommend conditional approval with the following conditions before full production access:

- Provide SOC 2 Type II redacted report (or full report under NDA) — this addresses control maturity for DataLakeX interactions
- Confirm encryption-at-rest and key management (where DataLakeX buckets are hosted)
- Add a contractual clause for onward-transfer notification: CyberLytics must notify Redwood 30 days prior to adding any downstream subprocessor that will receive customer identifiers
- Execute SCCs if any processing of EU personal data occurs through DataLakeX

If CyberLytics agrees, we can allow integration with a flag that prevents shipping customer PII to DataLakeX until SOC 2 evidence and SCCs (if applicable) are in place. Marissa — are we OK from a privacy perspective with the 30-day notification?

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Product Manager, Integrations
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morales <emorales@cyberlytics.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com, jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@cyberlytics.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 29 May 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: onward transfer permission and roster (CyberLytics -> Redwood)

Thanks Alex — we can accept those conditions. Attached is a redacted SOC 2 Type II from our last audit run and a short note on our encryption and KMS setup. DataLakeX uses AES-256 at rest and keys are managed in our cloud KMS with customer-side encryption support available.

Downstream note: we currently send aggregated hashes to DataLakeX and may engage a secondary processor (LogStream) for archived logs; LogStream is also SOC 2-compliant per their public attestations. We will commit to the 30-day notification clause and are prepared to sign SCCs via the DocuSign link below for EU flows.

Attachments: SOC2-Report-Redacted.pdf
Links: https://docusign.com/secure/sccs-sign/abc123

Elena
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <emorales@cyberlytics.com>
Cc: alex_martinez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: onward transfer permission and roster (CyberLytics -> Redwood)

Elena — thanks for the quick follow-up and for the SOC 2 redacted report. This thread captures the decision:

Decision (conditional approval):
- Integration may proceed with a configuration flag preventing flow of customer PII to DataLakeX until the following are completed:
  * Redwood receipt of SOC 2 Type II redacted report (received) — full report available under NDA if required
  * Execution of SCCs for any EU personal data flows (DocuSign link provided)
  * Confirmation of encryption-at-rest and KMS details (received)
  * 30-day onward-subprocessor notification clause added to the DPA (we will route a short addendum through contracts)

Next steps:
- CyberLytics: complete SCC DocuSign and confirm the LogStream engagement is covered by their SOC 2 attestations (by 2026-06-10).
- Redwood (Contracts): Marissa will send the short addendum for the 30-day notification and a single-paragraph limitation on PII flows.
- Redwood (Product): Alex will enable the integration flag and validate telemetry hashing behavior.

I'll mark this as an active compliance ticket (TICKET-14209) and re-open if any downstream changes occur. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Security & Compliance Analyst
Redwood Inference
